{{Quote|There's one place that we haven't touched, though-the Grand Audience Chamber at the top of the Temple. All of the instructors and students here agree that it is just too beautiful to change.|Luke Skywalker to Anakin Solo|<ref name="TGG" />}}
The '''Grand Audience Chamber''', also known as the '''Ceremonial Hall''' or the '''Temple throne room''', was part of the [[Great Temple/Legends|Great Temple]] on the jungle moon of [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. Measuring approximately 200 square [[Meter/Legends|meters]], the Grand Audience Chamber almost entirely occupied the fourth and topmost level of the Great Temple.

Its walls were dark [[Color/Legends|green]] blocks of [[Stone/Legends|stone]], and this huge room was considered an example of classical beauty. The Grand Audience Chamber was originally built during the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]] by the [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] warriors under [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]]'s orders. Along with the whole Great Temple, it was abandoned for 4000 years before being reinvested by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] and the [[New Jedi Order]].

==History==
{{Quote|Up you go, your worship&mdash;there's unfinished business that was a bit too lofty for the steps of the Ceremonial Hall.|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] to [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]|<ref name="DADS">{{StoryCite|story=The Day after the Death Star!|book=Star Wars Weekly 97}}</ref>}}
The Grand Audience Chamber was part the [[Great Temple/Legends|Great Temple]], a structure erected on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]<ref name="ANH" /> by the [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] under orders from [[Exar Kun/Legends|Exar Kun]], a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] who had enslaved them.<ref name="TSW6">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War 6|''Tales of the Jedi – The Sith War'' 6]]</ref> The throneroom occupied the fourth and uppermost level of the pyramid, complete with skylights and raised platform.<ref name="GG2" /> When Kun wiped the Massassi out by [[Force drain/Legends|absorbing]] their life-force, the Temple and the Chamber went into disuse for 4000 years.<ref name="DA" />

[[File:Medal-ceremony-Yavin-4.png|thumb|left|250px|The Medal of Bravery ceremony took place in the Grand Audience Chamber.]]
During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], it was used as a ceremonial hall by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] garrison. The members of the Alliance didn't refurbish the room with new materials, as they did in other parts of the Temple. They merely cleaned weathered debris and uprooted overgrown weeds, committed to restore the Chamber to its former magnificence.<ref name="ISWU">''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> In this very room, [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] presided over the [[Royal Award Ceremony/Legends|Royal Award Ceremony]], during which the [[Medal of Bravery/Legends|Medal of Bravery]] was given to those who partook in the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|battle]] over the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]]. For the first time in millennia, that vast chamber was full, with hundreds of rebel troops and technicians gathered together to celebrate their major victory against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="ANH" /> After the medal ceremony, a celebration was held in the Grand Audience Chamber, with [[Toast (ritual)/Legends|toasts]] coming often and exhuberantly.<ref name="DADS" /> During the Empire's [[Attack on Yavin 4|invasion of Yavin]], one of the minor battles that occurred on the moon within the six [[Standard month/Legends|months]] after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|destruction]] of the Death Star, [[General/Legends|General]] [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]] and several Rebel personnel were also trapped within the Grand Audience Chamber by [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]], although they were rescued by rebel heroes [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] of [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron]].<ref name="SW:RSIII:RS">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref>

When [[Jedi Master/Legends|Master]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] established the [[Jedi Praxeum]] in [[11 ABY/Legends|11 ABY]], the Grand Audience Chamber was used as a teaching space for the Jedi cadets.<ref name="DA" /> Unlike with many other rooms, the [[New Jedi Order]] left the Audience Chamber mostly untouched, as it was deemed to beautiful to be rebuild.<ref name="TGG" /> The Jedi would place rows of polished wooden benches and a small platform was positioned in front of the chamber for the speaker.<ref name="DA" /> Upon this, when Master Skywalker was in a coma because of [[Kyp Durron]], who was under the influence of Exar Kun, he was put on a stone platform on the stage of the chamber. He looked as if dead, which caused his students to feel grief and dismay. But with their help and the spirit of Master [[Vodo-Siosk Baas]], they were able to defeat Kun's wicked spirit with the Force. And Luke had awakened with his spirit back in his body.<ref name="COTF">''[[Champions of the Force]]''</ref>

[[File:JKAlevelshot_academy1.png|thumb|180px|[[New Jedi Order]] briefing.]]
During [[Second Imperium]]/[[Shadow Academy]] [[Third Battle of Yavin|assault on the Jedi Praxeum]], Imperial Commander [[Orvak]] set up his detonators in the chamber but he was bitten by a [[Crystal snake/Legends|crystal snake]]. Orvak woke up just in time to see what it was that caused his unconsciousness, and just before the detonators he set in the Grand Audience Chamber exploded. The explosion killed Orvak and destroyed much of the Chamber though it would be rebuilt.<ref name="JUS">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Jedi Under Siege]]''</ref>

During the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], the [[Conclave on Yavin 4]] was held here.<ref name="DTI">''[[The New Jedi Order: Dark Tide I: Onslaught]]''</ref> Later, during the [[Yuuzhan Vong]]/[[Peace Brigade]] [[Invasion of Yavin 4|conquest]] of Yavin 4, the Great Temple along with the Grand Audience Chamber was flattened by a [[Damutek]].<ref name="EOVI" />

==Layout==
{{Quote|Welcome to the Jedi Academy, Sir. Master Skywalker is waiting upstairs for you.|[[Jedi Praxeum protocol droid]] to [[Kyle Katarn]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight II: Jedi Outcast]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Grand_Audience_Chamber_Darklighter.png|thumb|left|250px|The throneroom consisted of a long aisle, complete with a podium and slit windows.]]
Measuring approximately thirteen by sixteen [[Meter/Legends|meters]],<ref name="GATORW">''[[Geonosis and the Outer Rim Worlds]]''</ref> the Grand Audience Chamber was accessed through a large wooden doorway carved with symbols that curved and twirled in a beautiful pattern.<ref name="TGG" /> The Chamber itself was a huge echoing room&mdash;according to [[Lore Keeper|Jedi Lore Keeper]] [[Tionne Solusar]], the acoustics of the Chamber were good for singing<ref name="I, Jedi">''[[I, Jedi]]''</ref>&mdash;the long sloped floor of which was paved with with rectangular slabs.<ref name="ANH" /> The slanted outer walls came together above the floor to form the room's squared-off ceiling. Most of the flagstones were a dull grey, while shimmering stone lozenges ornamented the chamber with bright ochre, vermilion or dark green.<ref name="ISWU" /> The high roof was equipped with skylights open to the [[Star/Legends|sun]],<ref name="GG2" /> and aligned with solstice and equinox.<ref name="IWSWT">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref>

At the far end of an open aisle, there was a raised dais reached by a flight of stairs made of fourteen steps. The back wall boasted five large window-slits that insured an abundant supply of fresh air and natural light.<ref name="ANH" /> Behind the dais, a small hidden stairway led to an observation platform at the roof of the Temple.<ref name="ISWU" />
When the young [[Anakin Solo]] began his apprenticeship, the stone walls were of a deep tan color, and they had worn smooth over the years. Electric blue [[blueleaf]] shrubs grew in the cracks throughout the stones and released a spicy perfume in the room.<ref name="TGG" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Luke, Han and Chewbacca enter the huge ruins of the main temple. Hundreds of troops are lined up in neat rows. At the far end stands a vision in white, the beautiful young Senator Leia. Luke and the others solemnly march up the long aisle and kneel before Senator Leia.|Extract from the final script of ''Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope''|<ref name="BTM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref>}}
The Grand Audience Chamber first appeared during the triumphant end sequence of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] in [[1977]].<ref name="ANH" />
While most of the interior scenes of the movie were filmed at [[Elstree Studios]], just outside of [[Wikipedia:London|London]], the triumph ceremony required a stage far larger than anything Elstree could offer. Thus, the massive Stage H at [[Shepperton Studios]] was used to portray the Grand Audience Chamber. The Rebel Briefing Room and the monitoring of the attack on the Death Star scene were also shot at Shepperton.<ref name="BTM" />

The filmmakers originally intended to use a matte painting to create the vast assembly present for the triumph ceremony. However, this proved too difficult, and the extras were filmed at the near end of the stage, then relocated into the middle and filmed again, and finally moved to the far end of the room and filmed one last time. During the filming of this final scene, the extras whispered insults and openly mocked [[Mark Hamill]] and [[Harrison Ford]] for starring in a movie that they believed would be a flop.<ref name="BTM" />

The layout of the Chamber has been portrayed consistently throughout the [[Star Wars Legends|Expanded Universe]], with only minor differences. For example, in the [[2003]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]'', the stairs leading to the dais are made up of eight steps instead of fourteen. The back wall also has several rows of window slits on top of another instead of the usual single row.<ref name="JKJA">''[[Star Wars: Jedi Knight: Jedi Academy]]''</ref> In case of inconsistencies, this present article follows the depiction of the movie, due to its absolute level of [[canon]]icity.
